quality_controls.overclaim_guard: No direct molecular pore mechanism is claimed; SEM is treated as direct morphology evidence and pore formation remains author-inferred.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Dimeric and tetrameric peptides produced visible bacterial morphology and surface/membrane alterations in SEM after 2 h treatment at 3x MIC.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: dimeric and tetrameric RRWQWR motif peptides
mechanism_claims.limitations: SEM supports morphology/surface damage after peptide treatment, not a fully resolved molecular mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper hypothesizes cationic peptide attachment to bacterial surfaces and pore formation as a possible mechanism for branched LfcinB-derived peptides.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Preserved as an author hypothesis grounded in SEM/physicochemical discussion; not promoted to direct molecular mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Increasing RRWQWR motif presentation and net positive charge is associated with stronger antibacterial activity in this source, while hydrophobicity/pI changes do not explain the effect alone.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: motif, palindromic, dimeric, tetrameric, and LfcinB reference peptides
mechanism_claims.limitations: Structure-activity context, not an independent mechanism assay.
